utterances.text: Okay. There is two sections. There is that when Trivic meets him, and he says, "On to Bratunac," and, "Colonel, we will talk about that." And there is another section where Mladic is doing the same thing, a little while later Pandurevic steps in and says something to the effect of, "Wait, general, we have to secure the hills because there is Muslims up there," or maybe -- and so that comes to what his final orders were, to secure the hills, and I think that's in agreement. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And I think we have seen that second portion as well, isn't it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So I wasn't playing it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But we can if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there is no need to do that. But we now at least have a clear factual basis for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the agreement but only that I agreed on securing the hills, so if it's not played today we will play it tomorrow for sure at the beginning of our ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you are -- of course, it's up to you to select what you want to play with the witness. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We may continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that the members of UNPROFOR crossed over to the side of the Army of Republika Srpska. Did you mistreat them, did you threaten them, did you torture them? How did you treat them?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: There were no threats. There was no torture, no mistreatment. In this group where I was, there was a soldier who was able to communicate with them in English. They said who they were. They surrendered the weapons to my group. And then all together headed by me we walked back to the command post in Jasenovo. Among them there was an officer who sat with me. We offered them something to eat and I know that we had a beer. It was quite a warm day and we managed to cool the beer in a stream. And then we headed. It is then that I informed them about what happened, and then a representative of the corps command appeared and took them over and led them away from my command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Via that interpreter, were you able to find out about their state of mind? Were they scared? Were they distressed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did learn about that. An example showing how scared they were was when they left the APC, at which time one of those young soldiers must have been in a difficult mental state and his trousers all of a sudden became wet. So we told them that there was no reason for them to be afraid, that they came into safe hands, and that they should not be afraid, and they should not worry that anything would transpire that would be in line with the stories they had heard earlier about who Serbs were, what kind of soldiers they were, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you via the interpreter that the members of the 28th Division used them as human shield?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: After all these years, I can't remember the exact conversation that we had. It's possible that something like that was mentioned in that brief conversation that I had with them. Later on, I learned that there had been such attempts. I learned that from the book written by the interpreter who was from Srebrenica, Nuhanovic I think was his name. I can't remember, though, whether back at that time they told me that. Later on I saw some documents and some statements and some combat documents from that time all indicated that they were told to take advantage of the positions of the UN forces, to take full advantage to their benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, that may be true or not, but what we are interested in to hear from you is not what you read in books, not and what you later learned in statements of others and what conclusions reading that material might justify. We are exclusively interested in what you heard, what you saw, what you observed at that time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you for cautioning me. When it comes to this instance of using UN forces as human shield by the members of the 28th Division, the only area where I saw that happen was the area of Zepa and Borik where they fired from the APC of Ukrainian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will get to that part as well, and we have a document that refers to that. Now, when it comes to the document that is on our screens right now, tell us, please, does it reflect accurately in paragraph 4 what happened on the ground about how those people were taken over?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, we tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D973 receives D288, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D288 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it the village of Slapovic or Slapovici?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I think that it's without the i. I think it's just Slapovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Slapovic. All right. So the village of Slapovic was empty when you got there; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The population was not there within those houses. Actually, this is a settlement of prefabricated homes. That's how it was established, if you will. There was no population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you reached that place, there was no longer any members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina there; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, there was nobody there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And not a single house there was set on fire; right? They were all intact.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No house was damaged by anything, either as a result of combat activities or any other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me asking you something briefly now about the fire that was opened by the Army of Republika Srpska before entering Srebrenica. You personally entered the town of Srebrenica; right? We can see it in the video footage that we'll probably show tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before entering, did your forces open fire on the town of Srebrenica, the forces under your command?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: The forces under my command, those units had no need to do that nor did they open fire against the town of Srebrenica. I'm saying this because our forces came under fire and there was no need for us to fire at the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During this operation, was heavy weaponry used at all? What kind of weapons did you have at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: In addition to small arms, the support weaponry that I had was one mortar, 82-millimetre, and perhaps another calibre. I would need to check my diary for that. And nothing else. As I said, we had small arms that we had on us. As for the three tanks that were -- that I had in my units, they had been resubordinated to the Zvornik Brigade due to the configuration of the terrain. It was possible for them to use the tanks if needed because that's what the ground was like in their area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the course of that attack, did you see other units of the Army of Republika Srpska or perhaps those three tanks themselves? Did you see them open fire at the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I did not see that and I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So now we go to the 11th of July, 1995, the entry into Srebrenica. When you personally - not your unit - but you personally entered the town, did you see buildings destroyed by artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I did not see damaged or destroyed buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the road to Srebrenica and in Srebrenica itself, how many dead people did you see?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I did not see a single corpse on the road along which I moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see any houses burning in Srebrenica or burnt houses in Srebrenica when you entered?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw shattered glass on the Srebrenica hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that. But it wasn't that there were ruins there anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not see any direct hits on the hospital itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1995, did you enter the UN base in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you enter Srebrenica? Can you remember the exact time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I have either the fortune or misfortune to have my own diary, so that often helps me remember, especially in such situations when I am preparing to testify. I think it was between 17- and 1800 hours on the 11th [Realtime transcript read in error "27th"] of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you enter Naser Oric's apartment on that day, too?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Me? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The civilian population relocated from Srebrenica to Potocari before you entered the town; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am sure. Most of them. Also there were still some individuals who were leaving those small streets and buildings and they were told that they should go to Potocari to the base there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I clarify about which day are you testifying at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 11th. The 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the record I see on page 53, line 15, "I think it was between 17- and 1800 hours on the 27th of July." I take it that you are referring to the 11th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say either the 11th or the 27th. I did not say anything about the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And in fact you were testifying at the moment about 11th; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for noticing that, Your Honour. I missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you personally help some elderly persons on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Then, we'll get to that when we start talking about the 12th. You or some other member of the VRS, do you know, did you find any weapons in any of the depots that the Muslims had allegedly handed over?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not find anything and no one informed me about any such thing and I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Members of UNPROFOR, did they hand over weapons to members of the VRS that they allegedly held in the depot? Did you hear anything like that or did anyone hand anything over to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, and I wouldn't want to speculate as to what I heard and when I heard it, but I did not know of anything like that at the time and who took these weapons and who gave what to who.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The only personal contact that you had with General Ratko Mladic during this operation or action was when you were filmed in Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the only personal contact. And the one at the meeting on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During this action, you did not have any contact with General Ratko Mladic, not even through communications equipment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There weren't any conversations. I just knew about the circular information stating that there could be NATO air strikes and that commanders should personally speak through radio equipment in such a situation, so it wouldn't be the communications officer or operator but it would have to be the commander personally who would have to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion in that circular information, the General is cautioning about the possibility of NATO air strikes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was a warning, and it was an announcement of that possibility, and that we should camouflage our forces, that they shouldn't be concentrated, that they should be extended over a broader area as is the case in such situations. So it has to do with what officers are duty-bound to do in such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he's just reminding you about the duties that had already been prescribed; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you enter the building of Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: You mean the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 11th.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No. The municipality building, I entered it -- or, rather, I was in front of the building on the 13th in the morning when preparing vehicles to transport personnel to the area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 4400 in e-court now. Just a moment, please. I need to approach my client.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see this document now, the 11th of July, 1995, issued by the commander of the Drina Corps Milenko Zivanovic at the time. In the first paragraph it says: "The command of the 28th Division of the so-called Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina asked to be immediately redeployed from the Sarajevo front." And then in the last paragraph in B/C/S, it's on the next page in English, it says: "In agreement and co-operation with MUP organs in Srebrenica" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "... Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, Sokolac and Zvornik, by sensible deployment of forces, ensure control of roads, block the passage of Muslims from and into the enclave and take control over the territory in depth in relation to the road." Did you manage to find this? We actually need the previous page in B/C/S. I do apologise. At that time is it correct that you did not have accurate information as to where the members of the 28th Division were. Also you did not have accurate information as to what their intentions were?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: What you say in your question is correct. We did not have information as to where they were and in which directions they were moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we clarify who he means by "we"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain, Witness, when you said, "We did not have information ..." who you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Army of Republika Srpska or, rather, the Drina Corps. But let me correct this by saying that I did not have information. My command group and I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account the possibility, in your plans, that is, that along any road that you were moving on within the enclaves or the enclave of Srebrenica at the time and around it that there could be an attack from the units of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That was one of the important assessments made, that one had to be alert and complete these active operations, which did happen on the 12th because we were given tasks to complete the attack, to enter the state of pursuit towards the facilities that were the original targets that were set for individual units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what we see on the screen, is this in line with what you and your unit received at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'd like to ask that this document, 65 ter 4400, be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D289, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D289 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like us to move in time, the 12th of July, 1995. In Potocari when you were passing by in the evening, you were passing by around 2030 hours on the evening of the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly, because I needed to reach the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw the police trying to maintain law and order and to keep the traffic going for the vehicles that were there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first evening --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a misstatement of the prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if there is any problem in whether or not it accurately states, could you please quote to the extent possible literally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D970, please, line -- page 16 in the e-court. [Interpretation] This is a page of the Popovic et al. trial and the page number of that transcript is 11838. [In English] I will read, quote, answer, line 3: "A. There were many people in Potocari, crowds of people. On the road itself, while I wouldn't say that there were crowds of people, but at any rate there were people moving along the road to the left and to the right roadside, and one had to pass through that section of the road quite slowly. Military and civilian police officers, several of them, tried to maintain order and make way for the vehicles passing along that road." So I don't know if the problem was with translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's "the law" which was missing, but, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now that it's complete and we have military and civilian police I think it's a fair question, otherwise I think it was unfairly questioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we go back to audio recording, I am sure that I mentioned military and civil police [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You have an opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise if that made confusion, but I am sure that I read both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first evening as you were going through Potocari, on that evening did you see any buses?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: The 12th?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I think I did see them but in that commotion one didn't pay attention to everything that was happening and much time has passed since. I know that of the 13th I was driving in a column of vehicles, buses, trucks, transporting residents from Potocari to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are still on the 12th. And there was a meeting of the 12th of July in the evening at the Fontana Hotel. You attended only one meeting at the Bratunac Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the meeting we are discussing right now, you mentioned in your previous testimony that you heard General Mladic talking about the need to provide fuel for buses and trucks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To ensure fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that meeting on the 12th of July in the evening, you remember that you were present and General Pandurevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's for certain.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Colonel Pandurevic, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't remember anybody from the Main Staff attended that meeting other than General Mladic; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember anybody else being there from the Main Staff other than General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that between the 6th and 13th of July, 1995, in Bratunac, you had no contact nor did you see anybody from the Main Staff of the VRS there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that other than the cases you stated, you had no communication with any members of the Main Staff during the Krivaja 95 operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I did not communicate with any officers from the Main Staff at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this meeting on the 12th of July in the evening was attended by General Mladic as well. At what time did he come? Was it at around 2200 hours?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he came at around 2200 hours. General Krstic came at 2100 hours and General Mladic joined at 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did he say on that occasion. Will you tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I can't quote his exact words but he congratulated on the results of the combat until that point. And as I have stated earlier to Mr. McCloskey, he gave a task -- or, rather, he proposed -- well, he asked General Krstic to come up with a plan for the Srebrenica enclave and how that was going to be solved, and he said that they should use the momentum of the success achieved until that point and to continue into the next task immediately from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was your position? What was the position of Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: The only activity that was planned at the outset of this task as we were preparing our soldiers for the task was to take part in the splitting of the enclaves and that was the motive for the soldiers and for those who came to participate. As you know, not all of the soldiers wanted or were willing to take part in the offensive, we assigned them to holding the positions and so on. I don't want to go into those details. And there were also some health issues with some of the soldiers because it was quite hot, there was no water -- not enough water, they couldn't bathe, and so on. So before General Mladic came, we informed General Krstic about the condition as it was at the time. That's what we did between 21- and 2200 hours. Maybe this is the first time I am telling you this, but General Krstic wasn't really willing to tell the commander of the Main Staff that we shouldn't go. He asked us as brigade commanders to inform him of that and to explain it to him. General Krstic did not know what the position of the commander of the Main Staff was going to be. We did inform Krstic earlier before General Mladic came and the conclusion of that meeting was as I have already told you today and as you already know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there an order to ensure the roads in the Srebrenica area at the time? Was there such an order?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to interpret things but, yes, there was a need for that, and as is stated in that document about closing off roads, it was stated there that it was necessary to maintain lines, positions, so that there would be no surprise attacks when the forces were withdrawing from Srebrenica. Yes, there was such need. And there was an order to secure roads so that there wouldn't be any surprise attacks in that area, Zepa and Srebrenica, as the forces were withdrawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there an order to secure roads leading from Srebrenica to Bratunac and Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were given such orders, too. And one of such orders was given to the 2nd Romanija Brigade given that such activities were conducted in their position. So there was no information as to the direction that the withdrawing forces were taking, so it was possible that they could have threatened the -- all of the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska in all of the areas through which the corps moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The order to secure roads was also issued by the command of the Drina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were in command of the entire operation and they -- and that's how it concluded, under their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that was a -- that is a routine military activity after an area is taken; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is a routine procedure that is applied always after combat activities. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The main task, at least as far as you were concerned, was to move on to Zepa; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. For me and my unit, yes. After the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that meeting, there was a dinner, right, on the 12th of July 1995 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had dinner in a room in that facility where the command of the Bratunac Brigade was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the dinner attended by the same people as the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were at the meeting and perhaps some other people joined as well among those who had organised the dinner. So it was in a separate room, not in the dining room of that facility. That facility used to belong to a company before the war and they had their kitchen and their dining room where the soldiers ate, whereas we went to another room where perhaps up to 20 people could be seated. So it was us from the meeting and some other people who had organised the dinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please listen carefully to my question. During that meeting or perhaps during the dinner which followed the meeting, was there any talk of the prisoners or possible prisoners or disarmed enemy soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: There was no talk of what to do. The activities concerning future tasks of the units mostly centred about what was to be done afterwards. And when it comes to closing off certain roads, blocking them off, controlling roads, and the deployment of civil authorities, military police, and so on, all of this was concluded -- the official part of the evening was concluded in the room where we had our meeting. After that, there was no talk of prisoners or disarmed forces. It was not discussed at the dinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it discussed at the meeting because you just said that it wasn't discussed during the dinner.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Everything that was said at the meeting was that somebody -- somebody with whom General Mladic had talked was to provide fuel, whereas the army was to rely on the old system of requisitioning vehicles to ensure vehicles, because I guess somebody was saying what about the vehicles. So that was all that was discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have now spent two or three questions on whether prisoners or personal prisoners or disarmed enemy soldiers were mentioned. Were they not mentioned at all during the meeting, in between the meetings, dinner, after dinner, before dinner? Was any -- but was it ever mentioned that there were prisoners or possibly prisoners or disarmed enemy soldiers? Clear question, please, a short answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. During that day at the meeting and during the dinner there was no talk of prisoners of war or disarmed enemy forces. All that was discussed was the evacuation of the population, evacuation of the Muslim population from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were not even mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that prisoners of war were mentioned or disarmed enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the evacuation of the population. Would that include men and boys of, well, let's say over 16 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that a question to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a question to you. You said that was part of the conversation and you talked about the population. Were you talking about men and women or men and boys or children and elderly? What was the gist of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wish to be clear. At that meeting, both the official part and the dinner part that followed there was no talk of prisoners of war. No such term was used, nor were the disarmed enemy forces discussed either. The term "prisoners" as it pertained to population, to people in Potocari, was used for the first time by the Prosecutor in this case when I was asked whether I had seen the prisoners, when I was asked about their evacuation, and so on. In that case I clarified it. I said that they were not prisoners and those who were killed. I said it back then that those were not prisoners and I wish to repeat it now. People in Potocari, the population, they were not prisoners. As for those who were disarmed later on on the road, those were the disarmed enemy forces and that was the first time I used that term, and I ask that it be treated in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I asked you whether prisoners or prisoners of war were even mentioned, you said: "I don't remember that prisoners of war were mentioned or disarmed enemy forces." So you started by saying that it had not been discussed and that at a later stage in your answers, after you have dwelled far away from the question and not directly answered the question, you then said: "I don't remember whether they were mentioned." Is that still your answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, when did he say that he does not remember? I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have, yes. Let me -- just one second, Mr. Lukic. It just disappeared from my screen, so I have to find it on the other screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The gentleman said that he does not remember whether anybody mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked, and we were talking about, evacuation of Muslim population from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Line 15, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] prisoners of war. I am looking at my question at page 65, line 14, and then the answer on line 15. "I don't remember that prisoners of war were mentioned or disarmed enemy forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not that he does not remember. He does not remember that anybody mentioned them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And earlier the witness answered more or less that it had not been part of the -- had not been part of the [overlapping speakers] that's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the same. I can clarify it with him but it's the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I disagree with you that that's the same. Yes, Judge Moloto has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At page 65, lines 20 to 23, Judge Orie asked the question: "That's a question to you. You said that was part of the conversation and you talk about the population. Were you talking about men and women or men and boys or children and elderly? What was the gist of it?" And you went on to answer, sir, from line 24 of page 65 right up to line 8 of page 66, talking about prisoners. Now, I would ask you to answer Judge Orie's question which wasn't about prisoners but about the population. Did you talk about men and women and children being evacuated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to try --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just say yes or no. Did you talk about the evacuation of the population which in discussion included men and women and children and elderly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no mention of evacuation at all. None at all except for the telephone conversation of General Mladic with someone about fuel for evacuation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It seems -- [Microphone not activated] Sorry. It does seem to me as if you -- there is a change from what you said, because Judge Orie earlier said to you: "Now the evacuation of the population, would that include men and boy of, well, let's say over 16 years?" That was long before what I quoted to you. And that was in reaction to you having said, "Thank you," and this is at page 65, line 10: "During that day at the meeting and during the dinner there was no talk of prisoners of war or disarmed enemy forces. All that was discussed was the evacuation of the population, evacuation of the Muslim population from Potocari." That's what you've just said. Now you say that that was not discussed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise to the Presiding Judge and the entire Trial Chamber. What you are imputing to me now is not correct. I did not say that there was any reference to the evacuation of the population. I never stated that and I'm not stating that today, either, that on that day at meetings or at the dinner that I attended there was any mention of evacuating the population, older, younger, prisoners of war, this or that, but I did say that for the people in Potocari, the word "prisoners of war" was used by the Prosecutor in Popovic, I think. And later in some statements I said that, after all, these were not prisoners of war. These were people who went to Potocari themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let the record show that I am not imputing anything to you and that I am not talking about prisoners. I am talking about the evacuation of the population which is on the record here, and if you say you didn't say so, and maybe it's just a question of interpretation, but the record shows clearly that that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This can be easily verified, Witness, by listening through the audio. If you say, "It's not what I said," then we'll check it and then we'll see whether you said it or not. Is that what you wish us to do? Or are you leaving the possibility open that you said: "All that was discussed was the evacuation of the population, evacuation of the Muslim population from Potocari." If you consider it possible that you said that, we'll just follow the transcript. If you say that's not what I said, we'll check it on the basis of the audio.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Once again, thank you. I do not wish, I mean, for us to have any kind of I don't want to say "clash" but misunderstanding. That evening on the 12th of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] No, no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- there was no mention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I am not seeking repetition of a discussion on the matter. What I'm doing at this moment, I asked you whether it's possible that you said what I just read to you. If you say, "No, that's not possible," we'll verify it. If you say, "It's possible," we'll leave it as it is. Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have this checked what I said. I want to be clear in my answers. And I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has got nothing to do with the truth. We'll check. We'll verify whether that is what you said. We are talking about page 65, lines 12 and 13. If it could be done during the break, that would be preferable; if not, we'll hear later and then we can put it to you tomorrow. We take a break and we would first like the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we proceed now? Do you have the right glasses?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the Fontana Hotel that evening? Did you leave when everybody else left? Did you leave earlier? Just tell us now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't know where we are getting the Hotel Fontana --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Bratunac Brigade. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your help. It seems that this entire misunderstanding is based on that first question during that part before the break. I did not attend the meeting at the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That has been corrected already. Please answer the question: At what time did you leave the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I left after the dinner and came to my command post very late.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you leave when all the rest left?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, did anyone at any point in time say or propose that the Muslims should be killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, no one. No one proposed that, no one said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time you had intelligence to the effect that most of the 28th Division was withdrawing through territory controlled by the VRS. They were fighting their way to Tuzla, that was under BH control; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time of this meeting, did anyone inform you -- did you hear about men being separated in Potocari on the evening of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that meeting and after that dinner, when going to your command post you passed through Potocari; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Potocari you saw women and men; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you paid attention to this, but did you notice the age of the men that you saw there? Would you remember that now?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember and I wasn't paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about the 13th of July, 1995. Did General Mladic address the troops on the 13th of July, 1995, and is it correct that he was asked to do that because of the exhaustion of the soldiers that had taken part in the Srebrenica operation before that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, General Mladic came to the area of the village of Viogor and he addressed part of the forces of my unit that I commanded, the unit that was commanded by Colonel Andric, and otherwise our forces were there in that area along that road in the village of Viogor. And this address was due to what we said at that meeting, that he would motivate the soldiers and he would mitigate the situation and motivate them to go to other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did General Krstic address the troops too?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, General Krstic did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he issue specific tasks to the units on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion -- or rather, after General Mladic's address, General Krstic addressed the soldiers and then he issued specific tasks to us, the commanders, in respect of Zepa, specifically those initial tasks so that we could move to the sector of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion what was the task that you received from General Krstic, to go to the village of Krivace; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the task that pertained to my unit was first of all what my marching route would be with the main forces of -- and then also what the dead-line would be for reaching Krivace; inter alia, it was stating that my unit would have a task, a particular role in Zepa and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now Potocari on the 13th of July, 1995. In Potocari you see groups of people, right, you see soldiers, policemen, and inhabitants of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: It was a clear day in July and I observed all of that that happened. I saw civilians, women, children, soldiers, policemen, men, vehicles, the boarding of vehicles, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now going from -- towards Krivace from Bratunac, you saw prisoners in Nova Kasaba; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Disarmed enemy soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were travelling by car; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was travelling, or rather, I was in my Puch vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not leave the vehicle on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, did I not. Except for lunch, but when I set out after lunch, I did not leave the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek some clarification of one of the previous questions and the answers. You said in Nova Kasaba you saw prisoners. Your answer was "yes." And then the next question was: "Disarmed enemy soldiers?" You responded again by saying: "Yes, yes." How did you -- how were you able to distinguish between prisoners and disarmed soldiers? Were they separate? Were they together? How were you able to see who was a prisoner and who was a disarmed enemy soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that there was a question with these two terms that I used. The forces in Kasaba were disarmed enemy forces, in my view, from the units of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] So there were no -- there were only disarmed soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Kasaba, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you know? Did you speak with them? Or how did you know that they were disarmed soldiers rather than persons not being armed, whether or not belonging to any armed force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would rather not explain, but the stage of the attack that we carried out on the 12th, which was the conclusion of the offensive, was the pursuit stage of the enemy forces that refused to surrender. Had they surrendered when they were in an impossible situation and had they stayed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- with their population, then they would have been arrested or taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm stopping you there. Again, you are not answering my question which seems to become a habit of yours. Simply, how were you able to distinguish between disarmed soldiers and -- apparently you consider disarmed soldiers not being prisoners, not even being prisoners of war. I do not know what your answer means in this respect, that there were no prisoners. But how could you distinguish between those who were not free, apparently, to move as they wished? How did you know that they were disarmed soldiers rather than not disarmed soldiers? Please could you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreter used the term "armed soldiers" and not "disarmed soldiers" in the last bit of interpretation I received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am talking about disarmed soldiers. Could you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer to your question is this: Those who I saw in Kasaba for me were disarmed enemy forces who had been disarmed at the conclusion of the attack in the pursuit stage. They did not surrender in the combat activities when they were in the position to surrender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Still my question is: How could you know that they were and, for example, not non-combatants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of them who had set out to break through towards Tuzla, towards the canton where they wanted to go, in order not to become prisoners of war, all of them put themselves in the position of being disarmed enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore your explanation is that if someone decided to try to leave the area through the woods instead of surrendering, that they, for that reason, were part of enemy forces. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of those who decided to set out with the soldiers of the 28th Division - I don't know whether all of them were members of the 28th Division or not, nobody knows that - but all of those who had set out to break through expecting to go towards their own free territory across the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska brought themselves in a position where they became disarmed enemy forces because the Army of Republika Srpska was concluding its offensive and was in the pursuit stage. Had they decided earlier on to surrender via their representatives, via their commanders, once they saw that they were in an impossible situation, then they would have become prisoners of war. This was my interpretation and the interpretation of the international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They put themselves in this situation where they became disarmed enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to you that that's your interpretation. Whether that's the interpretation of the international laws of war is for this Chamber to further consider. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When you pass by in Nova Kasaba towards Krivace, in your vehicle, how did you establish that these people you saw there, these detained people, were part of those who tried to break through towards the so-called free territory? How did you establish that, by passing by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] See here. In the course of those several days while the combat activities were carried out and while those events were taking place, the effects can only have one interpretation. In that period of time, one part of combat activities were concluded. On the 10th or 11th, somebody decided that the forces of the 28th Division and the population would withdraw from the positions. Now, whether it was the commanders of the local authorities who decided that, I don't know; however, some of them went to Potocari --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not my question. You passed by, by car, and saw a group of people, and then you established that these were disarmed enemy soldiers. How many people -- how many disarmed enemy soldiers did you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On 15th or 20 kilometres further on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, no, no. Please stop. I asked you a precise question. How many people did you see there? How many disarmed enemy soldiers did you see at Nova Kasaba, only there, when you passed by in your car? Please answer my question and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said at the football-pitch, at the football stadium, on the right side of the road as I was moving along the road, I cannot tell you how many there were. I didn't count. But almost the entire football-pitch was taken up by them. They sat on that pitch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in the clothes that they wore at the time. I didn't pay attention to what they were wearing. This was in Nova Kasaba. Along the road I saw several smaller groups of disarmed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am asking about Nova Kasaba. You explained that you saw them sitting on the football-pitch, and were they in uniforms or in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't pay attention to the clothes that they wore. I don't think it's important. They could have changed their clothes to fair better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How did you establish that they were part of the people who tried to break through towards Tuzla? How did you establish that? Did anybody tell you or did you ask them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, the order of the corps commander, the last one we saw in the Serbian language, stated that the estimate of the Drina Corps was that the forces of the 28th Division were moving towards Kladanj and Olovo - it said everything to me, the forces of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I notice that you are not able to answer my question. Mr. Lukic, you should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nova Kasaba is on the road to Kladanj and Tuzla; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that direction towards Kladanj and Tuzla and on the road to Milici and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the clothes that they wore, you said that you didn't pay attention. In the clashes with the members of the BH Army earlier on, were you able to see that a lot of them were armed but wore civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was such situations in earlier combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the existence of nonexistence of uniforms among the soldiers of the BH Army wasn't the decisive factor in determining whether somebody was a member of their armed forces or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't the decisive factor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking for opinion. You're aware of that, I take it? That it's a decisive factor --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I'm asking his opinion as a commander, whether he would establish the enemy through the wardrobe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what you asked, but I do not mind. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are close to the end; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you consider this -- that this would --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- finish an area. Could you tell us more or less where you are in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked for four hours. I am sure that I will finish in that time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood. Mr. Trivic, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether it's testimony still to be given tomorrow. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom, III. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will abide by your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 22nd of May, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of May, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.15 p.m.,
